description: A Sales By Customer download is always called the same thing whatever period it covers, so two files taken for different date ranges cannot be told apart once they are saved.
steps: Open Reports, then Sales By Customer, with the date range on This Month.
Open the three-dot menu, choose Download Summary (CSV), and note the file name.
Choose Download Expanded View (CSV) and note that name too. This was seen with Product Type Parts & Service and both locations selected, Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
current:
The two files were called sales-by-customer-summary.csv and sales-by-customer-expanded.csv — correct apart from the missing period. Nothing in either name says which range it covers.

The files themselves are right: each begins with a "Date Range: Aug 1, 2026 - Aug 6, 2026" line and a "Locations: All locations" line, so the information is in the file but not in its name. The name comes from the download itself, and both spreadsheet options behave the same way.
expected: The file name carries the period that was chosen — sales-by-customer-summary-this_month.csv and sales-by-customer-expanded-this_month.csv for This Month — and the PDFs are named the same way.
source: The files are named for the report, the version, and the active date range: the Summary CSV is sales-by-customer-summary-{range}.csv and the Expanded CSV is sales-by-customer-expanded-{range}.csv. {range} uses this map from range label: Today → today; Yesterday → yesterday; This Week → this_week; Last Week → last_week; This Month → this_month; Last Month → last_month; This Year → this_year; Last Year → last_year; This Quarter → this_quarter; Last Quarter → last_quarter; Custom → custom.
The files follow the same version-and-range naming as the CSV (S14-R14) with a .pdf extension
